topic: A person learns their childhood best friend doesn't remember them
text: I keep thinking back to our days under the old oak tree, how we'd whisper secrets and plan out grand adventures. I can't help but wonder if maybe I didn't pay enough attention, didn't hold on tight enough. Maybe I should have called more often, sent more letters. After all, time is a river, and some stones get carried away more easily than others. Now, seeing them, the look in their eyes—it’s as if they’re meeting me for the first time. I tell myself they're just busy, that they have a whole world of their own. But I can’t shake the feeling that I let something precious slip through my fingers, a memory that wasn’t strong enough to withstand the test of time.
